messages:
Maya S. (Support): forwarding from customer (FinApp) — they see SSE streams drop ~65s in, client reconnects and receives partial JSON twice. billing doubled. repro steps included, says they hit it on Dedicated in eu-west-1. request id: rwd-cc-87a2

Maya S. (Support): minimal repro they gave (pasted):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/gen?model=gpt-small"
# client sits, gets a few events, then silence, then connection closed by server with partial JSON payload (last event missing closing brace)
```

Maya S. (Support): customer note: when they reconnect, server returns remaining tokens+some duplicates. they say Node client shows ECONNRESET.

Arman R. (Runtime): thanks — couple quick Qs:
- is their Dedicated behind an ALB or using our L3 routing?
- can we get the server-side connection logs for rwd-cc-87a2 (accept/write/close events)?
- approximate token rate and avg seq len?

Maya S. (Support): they said ALB in front (internal). token rate ~60 tpm, avg seq len 400 tokens. attaching their sample server logs (redacted) — pasted below:
```
[2026-02-18T14:12:05Z] conn=34523 accept
[2026-02-18T14:12:05Z] write=ok bytes=512
[2026-02-18T14:12:20Z] write=ok bytes=1280
[2026-02-18T14:13:10Z] write=partial bytes=256 err=EPIPE
[2026-02-18T14:13:10Z] conn=34523 closed by peer
```

Arman R. (Runtime): that log smells like client-side backpressure: kernel write buffer filled -> EPIPE when peer closed. two possible failure modes we see often:
- proxy/ALB idle timeout drops the TCP connection because no bytes are written for > idle timeout (often 60s), while app-level logic thinks stream still active.
- app is streaming larger chunks and not flushing small comment pings, so proxies see "idle" and drop.

Arman R. (Runtime): short-term repro suggestions:
- ask customer to enable simple comment ping every 15s from server: send a line with ":heartbeat\n\n" to keep proxies alive. This is the usual "SSE comment ping" trick.
- in parallel, have them run tcpdump on the host to confirm last packet direction before close (we need to know whether ALB sent a FIN).

Jon P. (Eng-SRE): also add: check ALB idle timeout and Nginx proxy_read_timeout. ALB default 60s — if their chunk cadence sometimes goes >60s, ALB will close with RST. Recommend set idle timeout to 120s while we investigate.

Nina C. (Solutions): I can message the customer template for a reproducer (node/python). propose Node example (use streaming reader and small chunks):
```js
// node client: use fetch with ReadableStream
const res = await fetch(url, { headers });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){ const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if(done) break; process.stdout.write(value); }
```
Note: don't rely on high-level libs that buffer the stream invisibly (e.g., axios tends to do that).

Maya S. (Support): customer tried axios originally. they will try the node fetch patch and report back.

Arman R. (Runtime): longer-term runtime mitigations we should consider in case proxies are out of our control:
- server-side periodic write of a single byte/comment ping on every active connection with idle > 15s. cheap and effective.
- detect repeated EPIPE/EAGAIN patterns per-connection and mark as suspected-client-dead to avoid attempting retries that produce duplicates. basically, when write fails, mark connection terminal and ensure we emit final event with `status: partial` to logs so billing doesn't double-count tokens for replays.
- add per-connection last_ack and last_write timestamp to tracing, expose in Console.

Jon P. (Eng-SRE): +1 on last_ack/last_write. also suggest adding convoluted but helpful metric: "duplicate-token-rate" per request id — we can detect when same token sequence sent twice after reconnect. that'll help billing.

Maya S. (Support): customer ran node-fetch test and saw streams remain alive when we send comment pings every 10s. they said duplicates reduced but still saw occasional partials when their client crashed (OOM).

Arman R. (Runtime): if client crashes mid-stream, server should treat that as terminal — but we must ensure we don't double-bill. We need a server-side reconcile: when a reconnection arrives with the same session id, the router/ingress should detect an overlap window and refuse to re-stream already-billed tokens (or mark them as replay). Implementation ideas:
- session cookie + monotonic token-offset. on reconnect, client provides last-ack-offset. server only sends tokens after ack.
- fallback: on reconnect assume potential duplicates for last N tokens and provide idempotency window for billing (refund/credit flow).

Jon P. (Eng-SRE): actionable immediate checklist for Support to ask customer:
1) switch to node-fetch repro (we provided snippet).
2) capture tcpdump at host around drop and attach pcap.
3) provide ALB & Nginx timeouts.
4) try server-side comment ping toggle (enable/disable) and report behavior.

SRE-bot: Incident created INC-2026-453 for tracking dedicated/streaming-keepalive. Assigned: eng-runtime, eng-sre.

Arman R. (Runtime): I'll prototype server-side comment ping rollout (config flag per-deployment) + metric for writes-per-conn and last_write_ts. If we can ship a small patch this week, we can mitigate a bunch of these proxy-induced closes.

Maya S. (Support): thanks team — I'll send checklist to customer and attach the pcap when they have it. Marking for follow-up in the incident. :eyes:
